statements.t: We anticipate that these costs could remain elevated for the remainder of the year, impacting gross margin in future quarters.

We anticipate that further conflict with Iran and other geopolitical conflicts could negatively impact our ability to deliver products and services in certain markets, and continue to result in increases in fuel costs.
The increases were driven by the factors discussed above, as well as lower interest costs on our debt and higher expected asset returns within our defined benefit plans.

Our primary liquidity needs in the ordinary course of business are to: (i) fund normal operating expenses; (ii) meet the interest and principal requirements of our outstanding indebtedness, including finance leases; (iii) fund capital expenditures and operating lease payments; (iv) fund indemnification payments related to legal and environmental matters; (v) make expected pension, postretirement and…
Employee Benefit Plans In 2026, we expect to make contributions of $4 million to our international pension plans, $44 million to our U.S. pension plan and $17 million to our postemployment plans.
However, there can be no assurance that we will be able to obtain additional debt or equity financing on acceptable terms in the future.
We expect to utilize our cash flows to continue to invest in our business, people and the communities we operate in, as well as to repay our indebtedness over time.

estimates.t: Our most critical accounting estimates pertain to revenue recognition, inventory valuation, goodwill, pension, postretirement and postemployment benefits, and income taxes.
